pictures.scene: Mauve, The Return of the Flock — a great flock of sheep coming straight down the heath toward us in the failing light, their woolly backs packed shoulder to shoulder and filling the whole lower three-quarters of the picture in creams and dull golds against the dark brown heather, a single small white lamb standing clear of them in the middle with its ears up and its face turned to us, the shepherd a small dark hunched silhouette in a cap behind the flock on the brow of the slope with his crook laid across his arm, a low brown ridge of heath running right across behind him, two or three birds specked against a pale flat grey sky above, and the whole surface crazed with fine craquelure, but the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep, …
pictures.name: pd_mauve_the_return_of_the_flock

pictures.scene: Plockhorst, The Good Shepherd — Christ walking straight out of the picture toward us along a stony track with His flock pressed close about Him, a tall full-length figure in a deep crimson robe belted at the waist with a long pale grey mantle thrown over His shoulder and falling across His body, a soft gold halo round His long auburn hair, His face bent down and His eyes lowered toward the lamb He carries high against His chest in the crook of His right arm with its legs gathered in His hand, a long shepherd's staff gripped upright in His left hand, His feet bare on the brown earth, four or five sheep crowding in at the left with their faces lifted and one big ram pressing against His staff at the right, a thin bare tree and a green bank behind them, and a pale blue sky above, he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out, …
pictures.name: pd_plockhorst_the_good_shepherd

pictures.scene: Duccio, Christ before Annas — a tall gold-ground panel divided into two storeys of a pink stone house, in the upper room Christ standing quietly in the middle in a dark blue-black mantle over a red robe with a gold halo and His hands loose at His sides, hemmed in on both sides by soldiers in short tunics and white helmets with a thicket of spears behind them, one man flinging up an arm and another leaning in to speak across Him, the old priest enthroned at the left in a scarlet cloak and a white headcloth turning on his carved seat to argue with Him, in the lower courtyard a long stone stair running up the wall and a maidservant in coral pointing her whole arm at Peter, who sits by a little fire of sticks in a green cloak with his hand raised in denial among a close ring of nine or ten seated men in brown and white headcloths, but they did not understand what he was telling them, …
pictures.name: pd_duccio_christ_before_annas

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, a street gate in Jerusalem — a huge pointed stone archway thrown right across the middle of the picture, its honey-coloured masonry blazing in the sun above and its vault sunk in cool shadow below, a lamp hanging on a chain inside the opening and a white bird crossing it, beyond the arch the lane running away pale and hazy between overhanging houses, latticed wooden window screens and a shuttered oriel built out over the wall, a tall rough stone pier on the right with a fruit seller leaning out of his stall and two men squatting at its foot, the lane in front packed with people coming through, a bearded old man in a white headcloth and a long black robe walking out at us with his stick, a boy in a scarlet jacket with a dog at his heels, a knot of men in dark robes and turbans behind them, and the whole foreground a floor of sunlit yellow cobbles, i am the gate for the sheep, …
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Constable, Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows — a heavy grey storm sky worked all over in broken cloud with ragged warm lights breaking through it, the tall pale spire of the cathedral rising right up into the middle of it and the long white body of the church lit below, a great dark tree leaning in from the left edge and filling the whole height of that side, a thick bank of dark summer foliage running across the middle, the river lying flat and silver across the lower third with the reflected light of the cloud in it, a fisherman standing out in the shallow water in a brown coat and a hat with his rod bent over the stream, a little boat moored against the far bank at the right, and a bare brown spit of meadow across the bottom, i have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness, …
pictures.name: pd_constable_salisbury_cathedral_from_the_meadows

pictures.scene: Wierusz-Kowalski, Troika Chased by Wolves — a moonlit winter plain under a deep blue-green night sky with the moon burning through a haze of cloud at the upper left, a sleigh bolting away to the right with its horses at full stretch, nostrils flared and manes flying, one driver standing up in the back wrapped in a sheepskin with his fur cap on and his face turned round in terror, the second man crouched low over the shafts in a headcloth with a gun levelled back across the horses, a wolf shot through and thrown on its back in the snow in the near foreground with its legs in the air and its jaws open, two more wolves closing from the left edge, a straggling line of the pack still running in across the middle distance, a thin black fringe of scrub along the horizon, and the whole lower half a worked field of trodden snow and dead briars, when he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away, …
pictures.name: pd_wierusz_kowalski_troika_chased_by_wolves

pictures.scene: Millet, Shepherdess — a black chalk drawing on cream paper of a flock left to itself on open pasture, the near sheep drawn big and dark with their heads down in the grass and their backs worked up in dense crumbling strokes, more sheep packed away behind them in a long low bank that runs right across the picture, a tall stand of thin wind-leaned pines rising the whole height of the right side with their crowns feathered against the bare paper, a far hedge and a dim wooded ridge closing the horizon, two small herdsmen drawn in a few strokes away in the middle distance with their backs turned and already walking off toward the trees, and the whole bottom third scribbled over with tufted grass and low scrub, the man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_shepherdess

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, Adoration of the Mystic Lamb — a flowered green meadow under a pale blue sky, the white Lamb standing on a red and gold draped altar in the middle of the picture with a ring of gold rays round its head, blood running from its breast into a gold chalice set on the altar cloth, the dove of the Spirit hanging at the very top in a wide blaze of gold with its rays combed out across the whole sky, spires and a far white city rising on both horizons above dark massed trees, ranks of angels in white and gold robes kneeling in a close press on the grass at either side of the altar with their wings folded red and blue and green behind them, two of them swinging censers and others holding the cross and the pillar, a silver octagonal fountain playing into a stone basin in the foreground, and prophets and apostles in brown and blue and cream robes kneeling along the bottom corners with open books in their hands, then there will be one flock and one shepherd, …
pictures.name: pd_eyck_lam

pictures.scene: Memling, Christ Blessing — one enormous half-length figure of Christ filling the whole panel and looking straight out at the viewer, His face modelled in warm pale flesh with the long nose and the small parted mouth and the brown eyes set calmly level, His dark auburn hair parted in the middle and falling in heavy waves over both shoulders, a short forked beard, a burnished gold ground close behind His head scored with fine ruled rays and broken at the top corners by scalloped banks of dark blue cloud, and His right hand raised in front of His breast with the first two fingers lifted in blessing and the other hand coming up at the bottom edge, over a robe of deep brick red that fills the lower third of the picture, i have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again, …
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_blessing

pictures.scene: Jorg Breu, The Crowd Shouts Against Him — a packed knot of men pressed up against the picture plane and all shouting at once, a mitred priest at the left in a gold-jewelled mitre and a yellow mantle over a green gown with a fringed red cope, his eyes lowered and his two hands lifted as he argues his point off against his fingers, a bald old man in a black cap and a white fur collar over a scarlet gown with gold-embroidered black sleeves leaning in from the front with his mouth wrenched open and a rolled paper gripped in his fist, a second mitred head crowded in at the right, a shaggy black-bearded man with his eyes rolled up beside him, a whole bank of faces behind them yelling with their teeth showing under black and green and white caps and red sleeves, bare arms flung up and clipped by the top edge, and a flight of pale olive stone steps cutting across the bottom left corner, many of them said, he is demon-possessed and insane, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Hunters in the Snow — deep midwinter seen from a snowy ridge above a village, a cold green-grey sky filled right across with the black bare branches of a row of tall trees whose trunks run the whole height of the picture, a crow perched on one of the boughs, three hunters trudging away from the viewer down the slope with their backs turned, heavy brown and grey coats, long spears carried over the shoulder, a game bag and a powder flask swinging at the hip, a straggle of thin hounds with their heads down in the snow around their legs, a fire of straw burning outside a dark inn at the left with figures stooping over it, brown-gold farmhouses with snow banked on their roofs, hedges, a frozen millpond and a steepled town laid out in the white valley below, and the whole foreground a broad unbroken field of snow, at that time the feast of dedication took place in jerusalem, it was winter, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_hunters_in_the_snow

pictures.scene: Poussin, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery — a wide paved court in a city of grey ashlar, Christ standing in the middle of the picture in a blue tunic under a great scarlet mantle thrown across His body, His auburn hair loose to the shoulders and His head turned to answer, one bare arm reaching right out of the mantle with the forefinger pointing down at the stone flags, a long flight of steps and a round-arched arcade climbing the wall behind Him, flat-roofed houses with red tiles and a clipped bay tree in an urn beyond, a bare blue sky with a bar of cloud over the roofs, a woman in a white head-cloth and a wide blue skirt sitting hunched on the ground at the lower left with her face turned away, a man in a brown cloak and cap standing watching in the middle distance, and at the right edge two of the crowd pushing in with their hands thrust open toward Him, so the jews gathered around him and demanded, how long will you keep us in suspense, …
pictures.name: pd_poussin_christ_and_the_woman_taken_in_adultery

pictures.scene: Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — two figures standing close together against a plain dark stone wall that carries a faint warm glow behind Christ's head, Christ on the left in a dull red tunic with a heavy dark blue-green mantle over His shoulder, His brown hair falling loose and His bearded face turned gravely toward the young man, His open hand reaching away out of the left edge of the picture as He speaks, and the young man on the right in a silk turban wound with a jewelled clasp over his black curls, a cream mantle banded with gold embroidery hanging from his shoulder over a sea-green sleeved robe and a woven sash, his young face lowered and turned away with his eyes cast down and his hands folded in front of him, unwilling, but because you are not my sheep, you refuse to believe, …
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Charles Jacque, Shepherdess and Sheep at Fontainebleau — a flock brought down to drink at the edge of the forest in the last warm light, a huge rough tree trunk running the whole height of the left side with its dark leaves spread across the top of the picture, a strip of pale gold evening sky and a far open plain showing through at the upper right, the shepherdess standing barefoot on the bank in a white head-cloth and a white blouse with the sleeves pushed back over a long blue-grey apron skirt, both hands folded on the top of her staff and her face bent down in profile watching the sheep go by, and the whole lower two-thirds packed with her flock pressing past her, heavy brown and cream fleeces, a dozen heads lifted or lowered, lambs crowding in at the right, and the nearest ewes already stepping into the still dark water and putting their muzzles down to it, my sheep listen to my voice, i know them, and they follow me, …
pictures.name: pd_jacque_shepherdess_and_sheep_fontainebleau

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ enthroned in the middle of a deep blue almond-shaped mandorla ringed with small blue cherub heads, sitting on a bank of blue cloud in a pale blue robe bordered with gold, His right hand lifted in blessing and His left open toward the viewer, a gold cross-halo behind His blonde head and behind that a great star of gold rays and red seraph wings spread across the whole inside of the mandorla, burnished gold scored with fine ruled rays filling the ground on every side, ranks of haloed saints and angels standing on little clouds at the top and down both edges in rose and blue and green and black robes with their hands pressed together in prayer, two crowned angels in blue brocade at the lower left, a single gold-winged angel standing below the mandorla holding up the cross, and a dark wooded horizon showing along the very bottom, i and the father are one, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

lines.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.
Jesus spoke to them using this illustration, but they did not understand what He was telling them.
So He said to them again, Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.
All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.
The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,
just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.
No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.
Again there was division among the Jews because of Jesus' message.
Many of them said, He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?
But others replied, These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?
At that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter,
and Jesus was walking in the temple courts in Solomon's Colonnade.
So the Jews gathered around Him and demanded, How long will You keep us in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.
I already told you, Jesus replied, but you did not believe. The works I do in My Father's name testify on My behalf.
But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.
My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.
I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
My Father who has given them to Me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father's hand.
I and the Father are one.
At this, the Jews again picked up stones to stone Him.
But Jesus responded, I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these do you stone Me?
We are not stoning You for any good work, said the Jews, but for blasphemy, because You, who are a man, declare Yourself to be God.
Jesus replied, Is it not written in your Law: I have said you are gods?
If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and the Scripture cannot be broken,
then what about the One whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?
If I am not doing the works of My Father, then do not believe Me.
But if I am doing them, even though you do not believe Me, believe the works themselves, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.
At this, they tried again to seize Him, but He escaped their grasp.
Then Jesus went back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stayed there.
Many came to Him and said, Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.
And many in that place believed in Jesus.
